title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC unanimously (22-0-0) found the complaint administratively out of order and unable to be put in order because Benyola lacked standing, then dismissed it.
first_summary: The SJC found Mr. Benyola's complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it because he did not have standing to file a complaint against Central Florida Presbytery. He was not a TE member or ruling elder commissioner from a member church at the September 18, 2020 meeting when the Presbytery denied the complaint. The SJC cited prior cases and dismissed 22-0-0. The merits were not reached.
summary: The SJC dismissed Peter Benyola's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery as administratively out of order because he lacked standing to complain of the Presbytery's action. Benyola was neither a teaching elder member of that Presbytery nor a ruling elder commissioner representing a member church at the September 18, 2020 meeting when the Presbytery considered and denied the complaint. Citing prior SJC standing decisions, the Commission held the defect could not be cured and dismissed unanimously, 22-0-0, without reaching the merits.
